answer: Neighborhood Persistence Scoring. Each agent earns trust from the durable cluster of peers that repeatedly transact with it, weighted like rings in a willow. A cluster qualifies only if its internal edge density stays above a fixed marble threshold across epochs. Sybils form isolated cliques that never merge into the wider graph, so their scores stay near zero. The lagoon of established clusters absorbs only agents with sustained cross-cluster links. An attacker must fund real transactions to fake each edge, paying per-identity relationship maintenance indefinitely.
